messages:
jane.s: Heads-up — FinTrust POC wants a secure on-prem connectivity plan for Redwood Private. They asked for three things: 1) minimal firewall rules they can hand to SecOps, 2) whether PrivateLink or VPC peering is recommended for their topology, and 3) what source IPs we expose for egress when using our managed endpoints. Can SRE/netops advise?

alex.k: Thanks — quick summary from SE side: PrivateLink is usually the lowest blast radius (no cross-account route tables) and preserves customer control over egress. VPC peering works if they want full L3 adjacency but then they manage routes and it may expose more surface area. For a short POC PrivateLink + an internal proxy in their VPC is our recommendation.

samir: Agree with alex. A few concrete notes for their firewall team: we only need outbound TLS to our PrivateLink VPCE (or to our public endpoint if they choose NAT egress). Typical rule set: allow outbound TCP/443 to vpce IPs (or to 34.XX.XX.XX/32 range for our public region endpoints), allow DNS to their resolver, allow responses. No inbound holes needed.

samir: Example firewall snippet they can paste into their change request: ```
# Allow Redwood PrivateLink egress
allow tcp from any to 10.11.22.33/32 443  # VPCE interface IP (example)
allow udp from any to 10.11.22.33/32 53   # if using remote DNS (optional)
# If using public-hosted API via customer NAT
allow tcp from any to 34.101.200.45/32 443  # redwood-api-us-east region
```

alex.k: Regarding source IPs — if they use PrivateLink the traffic stays inside the AZ and the source IPs are their own host IPs (so secops sees their internal private IPs). If they NAT through a customer-managed NAT gateway the egress IPs are whatever their NAT uses. If they want fixed trusted egress from our side (we control IPs) that's only possible for Dedicated/managed-proxy setups; we can provide a small set of owned egress IPs for allowlisting under an enterprise contract.

jane.s: @samir can you confirm whether we should supply a list of example VPCE IPs or ask them to share their VPCE once created? FinTrust prefers pre-approved lists before they spin anything up.

samir: We should give them one of two options: (A) a sample VPCE IP block to expedite firewall change tickets (we label as "example" so SecOps knows it will change), or (B) we can provide dedicated egress IPs under a commitment (requires account team). For the POC I'd suggest option A + clear callout: "Replace example IP with actual VPCE IP before prod".

sales_ops: Note on procurement/pricing: if they want guaranteed egress IPs we need to move them to a Dedicated or Enterprise plan — that affects monthly commit and egress pricing. For the short POC we can keep them on hosted but they must accept dynamic endpoint IPs or use their NAT. I can pull the pricing delta if they ask.

alex.k: One more security Q — FinTrust asked about TLS/mTLS and cert rotation. Short answer: we support TLS 1.2+ and recommend mTLS for the strictest posture. For PrivateLink you typically rely on AWS-level connectivity + TLS to our endpoint. We can also do application-level mutual TLS if they require client certs (requires config on their side + provisioning of certs).

jane.s: Perfect — I'll prepare a one-pager for their SecOps with: suggested firewall lines, the two options for egress IPs, and the mTLS note. Can someone paste a short bullet list of the exact pieces to include?

samir: Bullets you can copy: 
- Use PrivateLink VPCE where possible to avoid cross-account peering.
- Allow outbound TCP/443 to VPCE interface IP(s) (example above).
- Allow DNS to your internal resolver; avoid split-horizon surprises.
- No inbound firewall rules required for Redwood-hosted model serving.
- For deterministic egress IPs request Dedicated/Enterprise egress IP allocation.
- mTLS supported; enable if policy requires client certs.

alex.k: Add: If they plan to route high-throughput requests, recommend they provision a small NAT or proxy with sufficient SNAT ports to avoid ephemeral port exhaustion during the POC.

netops-bot: validator: Remember to attach network diagram and VPCE/NAT subnet IDs to the ticket for faster review. Link: https://redwood-internal/conn-checklist

jane.s: Great — I'll drop the one-pager into the FinTrust folder and ping them. Thanks all :thumbsup:
